Stanley Kubrick.pattern: Candlelit Barry Lyndon on NASA f/0.7 lenses; one-point perspective; take after take until exact.

David Fincher.pattern: ~1,000 invisible VFX shots on The Social Network; 40+ takes, split-screened; camera moves only with the actor.

Denis Villeneuve.pattern: Real locations and built sets over green screen; sand screens on Dune; haze and slow reveals.

Christopher Nolan.pattern: Real plane crash in Tenet, real truck flip in The Dark Knight; Kip Thorne's physics for the black hole.

Wong Kar-wai.pattern: Finds the film while shooting; handheld with Christopher Doyle; step-printed motion; framing through glass and doors.

Roger Deakins.pattern: Few sources, often in frame; every light has a logical origin; one LUT for a whole film.

Emmanuel Lubezki.pattern: The Revenant: only natural light on location, one campfire exception; negative fill; long takes on wide lenses.

Hoyte van Hoytema.pattern: IMAX and 65mm film; infrared-plus-film rig for day-for-night; grain, halation, real falloff.

Greig Fraser.pattern: LED-volume StageCraft on The Mandalorian so the world lights the actors; sand screens on Dune.

Bradford Young.pattern: Underexposed, soft images (Selma, Arrival); rich darker skin without flattening fill.

Annie Leibovitz.lens: Portrait light that tells the story
Annie Leibovitz.pattern: Concept-led, researched portraits; large soft painterly key blended with ambient; staged productions.

Peter Lindbergh.pattern: Hated retouching; 2017 Pirelli calendar against the 'terror of perfection and youth'.

Steve McCurry.pattern: Waits for the moment; Kodachrome colour; the eyes as centre; 2016 edit controversy shows audiences punish manipulation.

Gregory Crewdson.pattern: Crews of ~40-50, months of prep, rain and dry ice, ~50 large-format frames per scene, refined in post.

Irving Penn.pattern: 1948 corner portraits; bare backdrops and window or north light; meticulous still life.

Joe Letteri.pattern: Co-developed Gollum's subsurface-scattering skin (Academy technical award): translucency sells skin and eyes.

Paul Franklin.pattern: Interstellar: Thorne's relativity equations became the black-hole renderer, then deliberate tweaks for visibility.

John Knoll.pattern: ILM supervisor on Pirates of the Caribbean and Rogue One; co-creator of Photoshop.

Rob Legato.pattern: Jungle Book and Lion King virtual camera modelled on an ARRI Alexa, operated on real dollies and cranes.

Dennis Muren.pattern: ILM's most awarded supervisor (Jurassic Park, T2); CG dinosaurs replaced stop-motion once they felt real.
